title: Java Slide 5
description: Practice test covering counter-controlled iteration, for and do...while loops, switch statements with integers and Strings, break and continue statements, logical operators, short-circuit evaluation, operator precedence, and printf formatting.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet is executed?
questions.explanation: A do...while statement evaluates its loop-continuation condition after executing the loop body, so the body executes once (printing "10 " and incrementing counter to 11) before the condition (11 < 10) fails and the final printf outputs "11".

questions.prompt: What is the exact result of attempting to compile and run the following Java code snippet?

options.text: Compile-time error: variable i cannot be resolved outside the for loop

questions.explanation: When a control variable is declared in the initialization section of a for loop header, its scope is restricted strictly to that for statement, so referencing i after the loop body causes a compilation error.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet is executed?
questions.explanation: The exclusive OR operator (^) evaluates to true only when its operands differ, so (true ^ true) is false and (true ^ false) is true; !q && p evaluates (!false && true), which is true.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet is executed?
questions.explanation: When count is 2, continue skips the printf and jumps to count++ (making count 3); when count is 4, break immediately terminates the for loop without executing the printf or the increment expression, leaving count at 4.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet is executed?
questions.explanation: The semicolon immediately after the for header makes the loop body an empty statement, so the loop runs for j = 2 and j = 7 (updating total to 2 + 7 = 9 and j to 12 in the comma-separated increment list), after which the standalone block adds 100 to total once.

questions.prompt: Assuming a standard United States locale, what is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet is executed?
questions.explanation: Because ratePercent and 100 are both int values, ratePercent / 100 performs integer division and evaluates to 0, making rate = 0.10 and amount = 1000.0 * (1.10)^2 = 1210.0; %-5s left-justifies "Yr2" in a 5-character field, and %,8.2f formats 1210.0 with a comma and two decimal places as "1,210.00".

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet is executed?
questions.explanation: In the first switch, matching "NY" adds 10 and falls through into "NJ" (adding 20) before hitting break; in the second switch, integer division 75 / 10 equals 7, which matches case 7 (adding 2) and falls through into default (adding 4) for a total of 36.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet is executed?
questions.explanation: In r1, || short-circuits as soon as (a == 1) evaluates to true, skipping the entire && subexpression so a and b stay 1; in r2, & and | do not short-circuit, so both (++b > 1) and (++c > 1) execute, incrementing b and c to 2 and yielding false | true, which is true.

questions.prompt: What is the exact printed output when the following Java code snippet is executed?
questions.explanation: The outer loop runs for i = 1, 2, 3, 4. For each i, j = 1 adds (i + 1) because break only exits the switch, j = 2 adds 11 when i is odd or skips both result += 10 and result += 1 via continue (jumping to j++) when i is even, and j = 3 adds 101, totaling 114 + 104 + 116 + 106 = 440.

questions.prompt: What is the exact result when the following Java code snippet is compiled and executed?

options.text: Compile-time error: assignment operator = cannot be used inside an if condition

questions.explanation: Assigning a boolean to a boolean inside a condition is legal. On iteration 1 (x = 1), flag becomes true, y becomes 7 (7 < 5 is false), true ^ false is true so y += 1 sets y to 8, and x becomes 3; on iteration 2 (x = 3), flag becomes false, ^ still evaluates (y -= 3) < 5 setting y to 5 (5 < 5 is false), x increments to 5, and the loop terminates because flag is false.
